item.title: Solar panels 10 feet above Massachusetts cranberry bogs revive farming and provide lease income
item.description: In Massachusetts, a groundbreaking approach has emerged as two cranberry bogs have implemented solar panels above their crops. This eco-friendly strategy not only cuts farming expenses but also creates extra revenue through solar energy production. The initiative fosters healthier soil and revives forgotten bog areas, ensuring ongoing agricultural yield. Supported by state policies, this dual use of land is paving the way for agrivoltaics and sustainable farming practices.

item.title: Michigan court overturns $1.55 million judgment against couple who backed out of home purchase
item.description: In an intriguing legal twist, a Michigan appeals court has vacated a $1.55 million judgment against a couple who pulled out of purchasing a home over unresolved ownership concerns. The court uncovered notable procedural errors in the trial, chiefly concerning jury instructions and discussions deemed confidential. Consequently, the previous damages assessment was overturned, and the case is now set to return to the trial court.

item.title: Australian court upholds A$99,382 award over neighbour's blocked drain flooding backyard and pool
item.description: In a significant legal victory, an Australian homeowner triumphed over his neighbor who contributed to ongoing flooding that devastated his land and pool. The New South Wales Court of Appeal upheld the initial ruling, assigning liability to the uphill property owners for inadequate drainage. They were ordered to compensate A$99,382.01 and to execute necessary repairs to avert further flooding.

item.title: Irish farmer builds solar farm on 1.5 acres, powers 150 homes while sheep graze beneath panels
item.description: In County Cork, Sean Keating, a dedicated dairy farmer, has innovatively transformed a portion of his land into a solar farm. This eco-friendly venture enables him to harvest renewable energy while still allowing sheep to graze comfortably beneath the solar installations. Expected to power about 150 households annually, this project showcases the critical support from the government and could potentially motivate other farmers to explore similar sustainable energy alternatives.

item.title: Shay Mitchell sells renovated 1931 Los Angeles home for $1.95 million, three years after buying it
item.description: Shay Mitchell has made waves once again as she sells her stunning Los Angeles home for $1.95 million. Originally bought in 2012 for $1.35 million, this vintage property boasts traditional Spanish architecture, enhanced by modern upgrades that made it highly appealing. The flourishing real estate market of spring 2015 contributed to its quick sale, paving the way for the actress to invest in a larger estate in the area.

item.title: Forgotten attic jewellery collection fetches £506,750 at auction, including rare 1905 Cartier brooch
item.description: A long-hidden jewellery collection from Worcestershire unexpectedly fetched £506,750 at auction, surpassing the initial estimate of £150,000. This remarkable sale featured over 200 items, captivating global bidders. Among them, a rare brooch and necklace attracted particularly fierce competition, reflecting their exceptional quality. Profits from this auction will be distributed among the heirs of the deceased owner, marking a remarkable conclusion to a decades-long enigma.

item.title: Nearly 200 unwanted concrete pipes and culverts were lowered into the Atlantic off Jacksonville in 2026; instead of being dumped on land, the pieces now form a new fish habitat roughly 90 feet below the water
item.description: Concrete pipes and structures have found new life as an artificial reef off Florida's coastline. This dynamic project aims to enrich marine ecosystems in the region's sandy ocean floors, driven by partnerships among fishing clubs, government agencies, and conservation organizations. The new reef encourages ecological growth and offers promising recreational fishing opportunities, with future assessments planned to observe the environmental outcomes of these developed habitats.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Michigan couple sought a house discount, but ended up fighting a $1.55 million court judgment
item.description: A Michigan couple's $1.275 million home purchase turned into a six-year legal dispute after they sought a $150,000 discount following an inspection. The failed deal led to a judgment exceeding $1.55 million against them. On Friday, the Michigan Court of Appeals overturned the judgment, citing errors in the original trial, and ordered further proceedings.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A 219-acre Florida cattle ranch facing development pressure was approved for a $20.15 million conservation easement in September 2026, allowing agriculture to continue while permanently restricting development
item.description: A 219-acre cattle ranch in Florida received protection through a $20.15 million conservation agreement. This easement is part of a broader initiative preserving over 4,500 acres of agricultural land. The agreement ensures that the ranch can remain operational while preventing future development. It reflects efforts to balance agricultural needs with urban expansion pressures in the state. Protecting this land is vital for maintaining both wildlife habitats and agricultural sustainability.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: In 2019, New Jersey completed the removal of the old Columbia Dam and reopened about 14 km of river; a 2026 study found juvenile eels, sea lampreys and American shad upstream after years of monitoring
item.description: Columbia Dam in New Jersey was removed in 2019 to allow the natural migration of fish. Recent studies show encouraging signs of recovery in fish populations, including American eels and adult American shad. Researchers monitored the river for nine years to assess the ecological impact of the dam's removal. The dam's removal also resulted in measurable improvements in water quality, including changes in temperature and dissolved oxygen levels.

item.title: Teen invents affordable wearable stethoscope to improve diagnostics
item.description: Kayley Xu, a Year 12 student, developed Aucura, a wearable stethoscope designed to enhance respiratory diagnostics and access. After recovering from pneumonia, she sought to improve traditional stethoscopes that have changed little over time. Xu overcame challenges by creating a model of the human torso to test her device effectively. Her design aims to be affordable for clinics in rural and underfunded areas, allowing better access to medical technology.
